saints.name: Pope St. Victor I
saints.title: Pope and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The first pope of African birth, who pressed the whole Church toward a common date for Easter…
biography: Victor I, an African by origin, governed the Church of Rome at the end of the second century and is often reckoned the first Latin-speaking pope, promoting the use of Latin in the Roman liturgy. He is chiefly remembered for his firm action in the Quartodeciman controversy over the date of Easter, urging the churches of Asia to keep the feast on Sunday with the rest of the Church.

When they resisted, he went so far as to threaten to break communion with them, though St. Irenaeus and others counseled moderation. His insistence on a common celebration marks an early exercise of Roman authority over the wider Church; he is venerated as a martyr.
saints.knownFor: Pressing for a universal Sunday date for Easter.
